_about: Markers for languages and recognised varieties of the Iberian/Lusophone area that are easily confused with Portuguese at the orthographic level but are NOT Portuguese orthographies. The detector uses these to RAISE A FLAG ('this is not standard Portuguese — do not auto-convert') rather than silently mangling the text. Markers are scored; a token/pattern hit adds its weight, and a language wins if it clears its threshold and beats Portuguese evidence.
_sources: Mirandese: Convencao Ortografica da Lingua Mirandesa (1999); Lei n. 7/99 de 29-1-1999
Galician: Normas ortograficas e morfoloxicas do idioma galego (RAG/ILG, 1982/2003); AGAL reintegrationist norm

mwl.name: Mirandese
mwl.status: Co-official in the Terra de Miranda (Portugal) since Lei n. 7/99 de 29 de Janeiro de 1999.

markers.note: word-initial lh- for Latin L- (lhéngua, lhuç, lhibro) — impossible word-initially in Portuguese (anchored to avoid enclitic -lhe)
the masculine singular definite article 'l' (l mirandés = 'o mirandês')

oki-barranquenho.name: Barranquenho
oki-barranquenho.iso639_3: por (no distinct ISO code; classed under Portuguese)
oki-barranquenho.family: Portuguese-Spanish contact variety (Alentejan Portuguese base + Andalusian/Extremaduran Spanish)
oki-barranquenho.status: Recognised and protected as intangible cultural heritage of Portugal by Lei n. 97/2021, de 30 de dezembro (NOT a co-official language). Its orthography (Convencao Ortografica do Barranquenho, Univ. de Evora + CM Barrancos, June 2025) is a DRAFT in public consultation, not a legally adopted norm.
oki-barranquenho.convert_note: Barranquenho is a mixed/contact variety, not an orthography OF Portuguese; turning Portuguese into it is translation (Spanish lexicon, clitic reordering), not orthographic conversion, and its written norm is non-final. Detect and flag only.

markers.note: aspiration grapheme: post-vowel word-final h for PT s (maih, oh, cruh, detráh)
aspiration before consonant (ehtá, pohto, buhcá, Ehpanha)

gl.name: Galician
gl.family: Galician-Portuguese (West Iberian) — the closest relative of Portuguese
gl.status: Co-official in Galicia (Spain). Standard norm: RAG/ILG (1982/2003). A reintegrationist (AGAL) norm writes Galician with near-Portuguese spelling and is the main source of false positives.

markers.note: standard (RAG) Galician uses ñ; absent from Portuguese
RAG digraph ll (vello, muller, cabalo); Portuguese dropped ll in 1911
Galician 'moito' (= PT 'muito'); weak on its own
